'''Treaties''' is an explainer page on [[SoapBox Law]], published at law.soapbox.community/treaties. It explains how a treaty is made, when it becomes enforceable law inside the United States, and the cases that draw those lines.

== Why treaties matter ==
A treaty is one of the most powerful instruments in American law: the Constitution names a treaty part of the "supreme Law of the Land." That power is also why so much pseudolegal folklore is built on top of treaties — which is why this page states the real rule plainly.

== How a treaty is made ==
Under Article II, § 2, the President negotiates a treaty — but it is not law on the President's signature alone. It requires the advice and consent of the Senate by a two-thirds vote. The page then distinguishes a treaty that is directly enforceable in court from one that binds the nation but needs implementing legislation before a court will apply it, and cites the decisions that mark that boundary.
